subject: Data formatting for GPA from define.sliders

messages.author: 2db356350753c5ea
messages.subject: Data formatting for GPA from define.sliders
parts:
Good afternoon,

I'm hoping you can provide some advice on how to properly format my data to proceed from landmark placement into a GPA.  I've been using Meshlab to lay landmarks on 3D models, which I've been importing into R using the read.mpp function.  I have a total of 41 landmarks per specimen, 31 of which then become sliding semi-landmarks (so 10 remain fixed).  To define the sliding semi-landmarks I've been using define.sliders as such:

define.sliders(MyData, nsliders = 31, surfsliders = NULL, write.file = TRUE)  
sliders = rbind(define.sliders(1:18), define.sliders(18:20), define.sliders(20:35))

And then I've been using the write.table function to output a .csv file of the results. 

From here, however, I'm not sure how I should be properly formatting/compiling my data for gpagen to perform a GPA.  I'm not finished laying landmarks on all of my specimens yet, but I have just over 200 in my sample (and therefore I'll end up with about 200 landmark files and 200 sliders files).  The output file that I get from the define.sliders produces a list of which landmarks are going to slide, but does not provide coordinates - I believe that's because the actual sliding will take place during the GPA (is this correct?), and if so, how am I meant to format/combine my data so that geomorph can read it properly to perform the GPA? I understand that gpagen can handle both fixed and sliding landmarks through the curves argument, but am just not sure how to make it properly locate the data.  

I've attached two .csv files - the landmark data from one specimen, and the output from the define.sliders function for the same specimen.  

Thank you in advance for your help!

Sincerely,
Marla


Marla MacKinnon, MSc
PhD Candidate
Department of Anthropology 
University of Victoria

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Data formatting for GPA from define.sliders
parts:
Marla,

the sliders definition matrix only needs to be made once, as it is the same set of landmarks that will be sliding during GPA for ALL specimens. Note that this matrix is just a table that defines which landmarks slide between which other two, with one slider per line. So, a line saying e.g. 5, 6, 7 says "landmark 6 is a semilandmark that will slide between 5 and 7", a definition that will be the same for all individuals. As you mentioned define.sliders, I am assuming here that you are taking about curve NOT SURFACE semilandmarks. If you also have semilandmarks on surfaces, you need to put their numbers into a vector to be used with the argument "surfaces" in gpagen.

As for the landmark coordinates, yes, you will need to compile those into a single object, e.g. by writing a loop to read all of your coordinate csv files and compile them into a 3d array. Then your GPA would be something like:

my.gpa.result <- gpagen(mycoords, curves = semi.definition.matrix, surfaces = semi.definition.vector)

Again, all semilandmarks are the same for all specimens, so they only need to be defined once.

Hope this helps

Antigoni
